reason: The premise is factually wrong and the inventory is wrong three times in four. PREMISE: the day's label IS written by a person in this product, and this field specifically. src/components/welcome/contextual-onboarding.tsx:384 renders a 'Date label' input, placeholder 'Wedding'/'Examinations', beside the date; src/components/app/your-work/your-work-view.tsx:671-675 renders 'Primary date, optional' and 'Date label, optional' as a pair on the workspace-creation form. Both persist to workspaces.primary_date_label (src/modules/timeline/server/db/timeline-schema.ts:499), and src/modules/timeline/lib/audience-timeline.ts:195 validates it as a required string, max 40. It is a WORKSPACE value, authored at onboarding before Timeline is ever opened - which is why review-suite-fixture.ts carries primaryDate above the projects array, not inside a project. So render-b.js:1474's literal 'The day' is a lab stand-in for an off-screen value, three lines below F.project.name = sibling.name, which stands in for the same way the project got its name; the lab models neither surface, and the seat read a prototype seam as a missing product capability. INVENTORY: driven end to end (owner-empty, '3 October 2026', Set the day, Add a moment, name it Ceremony, Done, Preview, Publish) the string reaches exactly two places, the horizon subtitle and the unfurl meta title - 'The day, Saturday 3 October 2026'. It does not 'lead the unfurl card': measured, .b-ogWho is 12px at y=313, .b-ogNum 64px at y=345, and .b-unfurlTitle is 15px at y=461, the card's penultimate line. It is not 'the whole of Happening now on the wedding morning': states.day (render-b.js:1701-1722) never reads primaryDate.label at all - it prints todayItems.map(m => m.title), a moment the owner named, and the fixture's match is a milestone titled 'Wedding day' (fixture.js:87). It is not 'the last row of the printed keepsake': .b-sub sits at y=393 of a 1040px sheet, above the gap note, the behind block, the printed URL and the footer. FIX: it would make the best screen in the set worse and leave the model behind. The empty state's whole claim is 'it is the only thing needed to start'; the fix adds a second REQUIRED field with its own refusal sentence between the owner and their first moment, to ask again for something the shipped onboarding already asked beside the date - and asking it per project re-scopes a workspace column, which is the data model and out of scope. The rename control is worse: horizon() is called by states.phone, states.desk and states.print as well as ownerSurface, and states.desk is byte-identical to what a guest receives by deliberate design, so a b-grab in .b-sub plants an owner control inside the audience artifact unless it is branched, which the fix does not say.
sharpenedFix: Keep the two words out of the artifact in one line, not one screen. render-b.js:1474 becomes F.project.primaryDate = { label: F.project.primaryDate.label, date: started } - at that moment F.project still holds the workspace's authored label, so the new plan inherits it exactly as the real workspaces.primary_date_label would, the literal 'The day' is never typed as content anywhere, and the first-run card reads 'Wedding day, Saturday 3 October 2026' like every other surface. No new field, no second gate, no control in the horizon, no data-model change. This is a one-line lab correction, not a build; anything larger belongs to /welcome/plan, which is not this engagement's surface.
